title: Is Wool Carpet Worth the Price? Pros and Cons for Seattle Homes
meta: Wool carpet is worth it in a Seattle bedroom or living room you will keep for decades, and a poor buy for pets, stairs and rentals. Wills Flooring weighs it.
keywords: is wool carpet worth it, wool carpet pros and cons, wool vs nylon carpet Seattle, wool carpet moths Pacific Northwest, best carpet for Seattle homes

blocks.lead: Wool carpet is worth the price in a Seattle bedroom or living room you plan to keep for 20 years, where nobody tracks in mud and no pet has accidents. It is not worth it on stairs, in a rental, in a basement, or anywhere a dog or toddler spends the day.
blocks.detail: The premium is all in the material. Installation is the same either way: $0.99 per sq ft stretch-in over pad, $30 per step. Wool costs several times what a mid-grade nylon costs per square yard, and it earns that back only through longevity and feel, which is why we bring wool, blends and synthetics to your Seattle home to compare.

blocks.html: Wool comes up in Seattle more than almost anywhere else we work. Queen Anne and Capitol Hill owners restoring a 1920s house want the material the house was built with, and Wallingford families want something natural in the bedrooms. Everyone who has priced it asks the same follow-up: is it really that much better? Wool is better at some things and clearly worse at others. Here is the list, with no salesmanship either way.

blocks.text: What wool does better than any synthetic

items.title: Resilience
items.text: Wool fibers are naturally crimped and spring back after furniture and traffic. A 15-year-old wool carpet often still looks full where a same-age polyester has matted flat.

items.title: Moisture regulation
items.text: Wool absorbs and releases humidity without feeling damp, which matters in a city that sits above 70 percent humidity most of the year. It takes the clammy edge off a bedroom in November.

items.title: Depth of color
items.text: Wool takes dye deep into the fiber and reads richer and more matte than synthetics. In flat Seattle winter light, that softness is what people notice walking in.

items.title: Low VOC and naturally flame resistant
items.text: Wool is sheared, spun and dyed. No petroleum in the fiber, very little odor in a new install, and it is hard to ignite without added chemistry.

items.title: Right for the house
items.text: Craftsman and Tudor homes in Ballard and Queen Anne were carpeted in wool originally. For a period restoration, nothing else looks the same.

blocks.text: Price your Seattle carpet job right now

blocks.html: Here is the part people are surprised by: wool costs no more to install. Labor is $0.99 per sq ft stretch-in over pad, $1.29 glue-down and $30 per step, with a 500 sq ft minimum, whatever fiber is on the roll. Tear-out and haul-away is $0.45 per sq ft, moving furniture $0.25. Two bedrooms and a living room at 800 sq ft in a Wallingford house is 800 × $0.99 = $792 in labor, plus $360 of tear-out, and that does not change when you swap the sample from nylon to wool. The wool and its pad are quoted at the free in-home estimate, and that is where the entire premium lives.

blocks.note: The labor figure is fiber-blind. Ask us to price the same rooms in wool, in an 80/20 blend and in nylon to see the gap.

b.title: Choose it for
items: Any room with a dog or cat
Rentals and homes you will sell soon

blocks.html: Wool blends, usually 80 percent wool and 20 percent nylon, are the compromise most Seattle families land on: nylon adds abrasion resistance at the wear points, the wool keeps the look and hand, and the material price sits in between. Our fiber comparison goes deeper on each one.

blocks.text: What drives the price of a wool carpet job

items.text: 100 percent New Zealand wool in a dense loop or cut pile is the top. Blends and lighter face weights bring the material cost down sharply.
Wool is often woven narrower than synthetics, so seams and waste change with the room. A 12 by 14 bedroom cuts cleanly; an L-shaped living room does not.
Stairs are $30 per step, the most hand-work in any carpet job. With wool we usually suggest a matching nylon or a runner instead.
Wool deserves a dense pad. A cheap one lets the backing flex and shortens the life of an expensive carpet.
Old carpet and pad removal is $0.45 per sq ft with haul-away. Third-floor walk-ups, Capitol Hill parking and condo elevator windows get looked at during the estimate.

blocks.text: When wool is the wrong buy

blocks.title: Be honest about your household:
blocks.text: If you have a dog under two, a cat with a history, a toddler, or a West Seattle basement family room with any moisture history, wool will disappoint you. The stain and odor risk outweighs the fiber's virtues, and a good nylon will look better in five years. We would rather sell you the right carpet than the expensive one.

items.html: Pets that have accidents. Urine bonds with wool protein and, unlike solution-dyed nylon, cannot be fully cleaned out.
Basements and slab rooms. Wool on a damp slab means odor and eventually mildew.
Rentals and short holds. You never see the 20-year payoff, and a buyer will not pay you back.
Sunrooms and big south windows. The fade is permanent.
A tight whole-house budget. Wool everywhere usually means thin wool everywhere. Better: wool in two rooms, quality nylon in the rest.

blocks.text: How to buy wool carpet well in Seattle

items: Ask for the wool percentage, the face weight and whether it is moth-treated. All three are on the spec sheet.
See it in your own light. Wool shifts color more than synthetics between showroom LEDs and a gray Seattle afternoon.
Put a full-size sample on the floor for a day and walk it in socks. The hand of wool is the reason to buy it.
Pair it with a dense pad and get the spec in writing.
Plan the stairs separately, at $30 per step. A matching nylon or a bound runner saves the wool where it would wear.
Book a cleaner with wool experience before you need one, and vacuum with suction only.
Get a written quote listing carpet, pad, removal and stairs as separate lines from an installer who backs the seams with a workmanship warranty.

faq.q: Is wool carpet really worth the extra money?
faq.a: In the right room, yes. Wool holds its pile and color for 20 years, feels better underfoot and regulates humidity in a damp Seattle house. The extra money is all material, since labor is $0.99 per sq ft either way. In a room with pets or heavy traffic, a good nylon is the smarter spend.

faq.q: Does wool carpet have problems with moths in Seattle?
faq.a: It can. Clothes moths and carpet beetles like undisturbed wool, typically under furniture that never moves and along closet edges. Most quality wool is moth-treated at the mill, and regular vacuuming of edges keeps it from becoming an issue.

faq.q: Is wool carpet good for people with allergies?
faq.a: Generally yes. Wool traps dust until it is vacuumed rather than releasing it, gives off very little odor when new, and resists dust mites better than many synthetics because it stays drier. Anyone with a true wool sensitivity should test a sample first.

faq.q: Can wool carpet go on stairs?
faq.a: It can, but it wears at the nosings faster than nylon on a busy stair. In most Seattle homes we suggest a matching nylon for the stairs, or a bound wool runner that can be replaced on its own. Labor is $30 per step either way, so the choice is about the material and how long it lasts.

faq.q: How do I clean wool carpet?
faq.a: Vacuum with suction only or a gentle brush setting, blot spills immediately with water and a wool-safe cleaner, and hire a professional who works with wool for periodic cleaning. Over-wetting, alkaline cleaners and rental steam machines can brown, shrink or felt the fiber.

faq.q: What is a wool blend carpet?
faq.a: Usually 80 percent wool and 20 percent nylon. The nylon adds abrasion resistance where feet turn, while the wool provides the look, softness and moisture handling. Blends cost less than pure wool and are the most common wool choice for Seattle families.
